blender_capabilities.eevee_headless_note: EEVEE Next (4.x) requires an OpenGL/GPU context; fails in --background on integrated graphics without virtual display

workbench.note: First-frame overhead is GPU context init; subsequent frames are fast

eevee.result: FAILED — requires display/GPU context in background mode
eevee.note: Blender 4.x EEVEE Next requires an active GPU/OpenGL context. Not usable headless without Mesa/offscreen workaround.

cycles_cpu.note: All 60 frames completed successfully. High variance due to thermal throttling on i7-8650U. At 32 samples per frame, quality is acceptable for cartoon rendering.

ffmpeg_test.note: FFmpeg 9.0.2 successfully assembled frames into 5-second MP4

dependency_audit.mesa_llvmpipe: NOT INSTALLED (would enable headless EEVEE via software GL)
dependency_audit.pillow: NOT TESTED (not required for Blender rendering)

recommendation.reason: Workbench is fully headless-compatible, renders a 640x360 frame in ~0.13s steady-state (10.4s for 60 frames), and produces visually acceptable cartoon-style output with flat shading and solid colors. It is the only engine that works reliably in background/automation mode on this hardware.
recommendation.secondary_reason: Cycles CPU works headless and produces photorealistic output, but at ~20s/frame it is 150x slower than Workbench. Acceptable only for final 'hero shot' single frames, not interactive or batch animation.
recommendation.avoid_eevee: EEVEE Next (Blender 4.x) fails headless without Mesa or a virtual display. Do not use for automated rendering unless a virtual framebuffer (e.g., Xvfb on WSL2) is configured.
recommendation.cartoon_suitability: GOOD — Workbench with Flat shading, solid colors, and optional outline/cavity settings is well-suited to cartoon animation. The i7-8650U can render a 1-minute cartoon (720 frames) in approximately 2 minutes at 640x360.
recommendation.verdict: FEASIBLE for simple 3D cartoon animation at 640x360 or 720p using Blender Workbench engine.
